findings.text: The first paragraph works. A newcomer learns what Athena is, who it is for and what problem it solves before reading anything else.
findings.source: "Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository. ... It solves the problem of AI edits that arrive unreviewed and unaccountable."

findings.text: The page links to the next step from the top, and Next steps gives concrete commands, prerequisites and a sample first request. A newcomer knows what to do next.
findings.source: "Next step: install Athena or read firstmate itself." and the Next steps section ("git clone ...", "./setup.sh", "athena ask \"add a changelog\"")

findings.text: This is the only section that would show Athena's own output, the models, verdict and cost the lede promises, and it shows an internal error instead. It sits just before "Start here", so a newcomer meets a broken demo of the main selling point early.
findings.source: Check it on a real job: "The records of job 20261029-073603-7kqv could not be read here, so no models, verdict or costs are shown: no reading record for job 20261029-073603-7kqv."

findings.text: Almost all of the page explains firstmate, a different project, in great detail. Someone who came to learn about Athena has to infer that this study is the demo. The page never shows the request or command that produced the study, or what running it cost.
findings.source: Title "Athena explains how firstmate handles work" and the sections States, Counters, Transitions, Why it is built this way and Claims and sources

findings.text: This link appears in the header with no explanation. A newcomer cannot tell who the owner is or whether it applies to them.
findings.source: "Owner view: proposals waiting for your decision."

findings.text: Rust and cargo are mentioned but are not listed as prerequisites, so it is unclear whether setup.sh installs them. The lede promises "one AI model do the work and a different one check it", but the only AI tool listed is Claude Code, and the page never says what account or key is needed.
findings.source: Next steps prerequisites: "a C linker (cc), which cargo needs to build Athena"; "Claude Code, or npm to install it."

findings.text: Even the default core track uses exit codes, locks and "guarded fast-forward". It is precise and every claim is cited, but it is heavy for a first visit. A newcomer who only wants to judge Athena gets little from it.
findings.source: Start here: "If every place of a declared capacity is held, the spawn exits 75 and the item stays queued."

findings.text: This is internal build detail with no context. A visitor cannot see or use that folder from the page.
findings.source: About this page: "the name of the folder under studies/ that holds the data this page is generated from."
